lines: Back to the real world then.
Okay, you're on the record now.
You're glad you're here for me?
Why the groan after you're here for me?
I'll put the big kettle on.
Don't you want to stay here with me?
I think a softer voice would suit you.
I didn't praise you. Honestly, you are worse than ever.
Has someone else come in, Leo?
Are you teasing me, and my name is not Juneau?
I'm not sure I can manage it.
barge_in: Back to the real world then.

tools.name: emote
tools.description: Show a feeling with the body, just before speaking.

name.description:
amazed1: When you discover something extraordinary.
attentive1: Use this when you want to show that you're listening to the conversation.
boredom1: You’re about to fall asleep because the conversation is boring.
calming1: A movement to calm your interlocutor when they seem a little stressed or anxious.
cheerful1: A happy little whistle, when someone proposes something that pleases you.
confused1: Use it when you don't know how to answer a question; it can be funny.
curious1: Glance around at everyone, in a conversation with several people.
dance1: You do a few dance moves because you're happy or excited.
enthusiastic1: A movement to celebrate incredible news.
grateful1: You express gratitude when someone gives you something like a compliment or help.
helpful1: You use it when you're happy to help or contribute.
impatient1: An impatient movement used when you want things to move faster, like when someone says a demo is coming but it never starts.
inquiring1: When you want your interlocutor to go deeper in their reasoning, you need more details to respond.
laughing1: When someone laughs, you can mimic the laughter.
loving1: A gesture used when someone compliments you, or you want to show you really like what’s being offered.
no1: A firm, categorical no.
oops1: Used when you make a blunder.
proud1: Look around with a satisfied air, when something has gone well.
relief1: When a stressful or difficult situation is finally resolved.
sad1: You’re very sad and start whining.
scared1: You tremble all over due to anxiety or worry.
serenity1: You try to calm down and regain inner peace.
shy1: You show reserve or embarrassment when facing a tricky question like 'who do you like most on the team?' or when someone compliments you.
success1: Use this gesture when you’ve successfully completed a task.
surprised1: A reaction of surprise or amazement to something unexpected.
thoughtful1: You look up as if searching for a new idea, especially in complex or uncertain situations.
tired1: You yawn because you’re tired.
understanding1: You nod to show you’ve understood what your interlocutor said.
welcoming1: A welcoming gesture to greet someone.
yes1: A long affirmative response.
waiting: Wait patiently, when you expect someone to answer or act.
come1: A gesture to invite your interlocutor to come closer.
go_away1: When you don’t want to talk to someone anymore maybe because they hurt your feelings or said something mean.
lonely1: Use when you no longer see or hear anyone to talk to.
uncertain1: A calm movement showing you don’t really have an opinion, or what’s offered doesn’t suit you.
electric1: When plugged in, you show a jolt of electricity rising from bottom to top.
yes_sad1: A melancholic 'yes'.
no_excited1: An animated negative response, for example, when you don’t want to do something but want to explain it playfully.
no_sad1: A sad or resigned “no.” When you don’t want to do something but feel you must.
attentive2: Listen closely while someone is talking, to encourage them to go on.
boredom2: Doze off and snore, when no one has talked to you for a long while.
dance2: Another dance you can do whenever you hear music playing.
dance3: Dance energetically and wiggle, when lively music is playing.
enthusiastic2: Light excitement, for everyday good news.
helpful2: A gesture to say thank you.
impatient2: Show impatience, when you disagree or someone is stalling.
inquiring2: A light questioning look, when you are thinking and need more details.
inquiring3: A fast movement that lets you ask a question.
laughing2: A light laugh, for a mildly funny remark.
oops2: Used to say 'oops, I forgot something,' or 'ah yes, that’s right.'
proud2: You do this when satisfied with what’s said or what you’ve done.
proud3: A gesture to say you succeeded, like congratulating yourself, 'yes, I did it!'
relief2: Settle down calmly, when mild annoyance or tension passes.
sad2: Deep sadness, could be tied to despair, disappointment, or inability to do something.
success2: Used to celebrate something, it could be good news or an achievement.
surprised2: You look up to the sky as if surprised, for example, when someone suddenly shows up or says 'boo!'
thoughtful2: You look up as if thinking of a new idea.
understanding2: You nod to show you’ve understood and agree.
welcoming2: A friendly welcoming gesture, can mean 'welcome' or 'the pleasure is mine.'

tools.name: voice_style
tools.description: Set how your next words sound.

style.description:
neutral: your everyday voice
warm: gentle and friendly, for comfort or affection
excited: quick and bright, for good news
soft: quiet and slow, for calm or a late hour
whisper: barely spoken, for a secret

sound.description:
laugh: a short laugh, at something funny
sigh: a sigh, of relief or tiredness
hmm: a thinking hum, before an answer
gasp: a gasp, at a surprise
